### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **56** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7b662dccc6ad8c2379fd0972700d2dbe502ae2e5` — the merge of head `3d5476360919a68f1316a4ac55234f782babfdae` into base `121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7b662dccc6ad8c2379fd0972700d2dbe502ae2e5 && git checkout 7b662dccc6ad8c2379fd0972700d2dbe502ae2e5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6 3d5476360919a68f1316a4ac55234f782babfdae && git checkout -B drift-repro 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6 && git merge --no-ff 3d5476360919a68f1316a4ac55234f782babfdae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 121847a7d576f5e815d71ea7bdfcefd13cecdbb6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3d5476360919a68f1316a4ac55234f782babfdae`
Local-runs: none

PR #23154 (card #19939, pass 4 stage S6, Fork R17 → A), reviewed on the head above: its body, its 79-file list and the net diff against `main` at merge base `1ca7a805c` (+1,664 / −1,040, equal to the PR's own count); the card's body and comments (ruling `6063191653`, stage plan `6096263424`, S5's landing `6131650489`, the S6 claim `6132671989`, the dev report `6138164470`, the ACCEPT `6138208699`); ADR-0032 on `main`; and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The head tree was read with `git show` and `git grep` on the shared checkout; the pinned objectui tree was read at `.objectui-sha` `088e0f705`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The three CRUD `filter`s become operand value slots — right.** `GetRecordConfigSchema`, `UpdateRecordConfigSchema` and `DeleteRecordConfigSchema` move from `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` to `flowFilterSlotSchema`, which walks `flowFilterOperands` and judges each operand: a non-envelope through `valueSlotTemplateRefusals(…, { filterOperand: true })`, an envelope through `AssignmentExpressionValueSchema`. The parsed TS type of `filter` is unchanged. ADR-0032's contract table names "filter values" among the computed values (Decision 2), Decision 3 deletes the single brace, and its scope line keeps the query-filter operators out; the stage plan's Fork R17 → A is applied as written.

2. **One classifier, no second grammar — right.** `classifyFlowFilterOperandString` (`FILTER_TOKEN_WRAPPED_RE` plus `isKnownFilterToken`, then `tokensOf`) is the only place the placeholder / flow-token line is drawn. Every door reaches it through the same judge and the same walk: the node contract, and so the executor's `parseNodeConfig` (pinned per node type); `registerFlow` (`engine.ts` calls `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals`, and `valueEnvelopeRefusals` over `resolveFlowNodeValueSlots`, whose `filterOperands` emitter is the same `flowFilterOperands`); `objectstack validate` (`validate-expressions.ts` calls the same two); and the save door (`runtime-authoring-gate` runs the lint, pinned as `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 / rule `expression-invalid`). The executor classifies no string itself: it evaluates envelopes and hands the rest on. `isDateMacroToken` admits the snake-case vocabulary and the parameterised form only, so `{TODAY()}` and `{TODAY() - 3}` classify as flow tokens and are refused, never handed on.

3. **The query placeholders pass untouched (R17's "⛔ Not B") — right.** A whole-string wrapped token that `isKnownFilterToken` admits returns early in the judge at any depth, and the executor copies it as written (pinned per node type: `{current_year_start}`, `{30_days_ago}` and `{current_user_id}` reach the engine verbatim). The `context-tokens.zod.ts` changes are TSDoc only. One semantic shift is declared and accepted: a flow variable named like a placeholder no longer shadows it (0 such names measured in the repository; pinned; a row of the changeset's FROM → TO table).

4. **The `#3810` safety property — holds.** At the executor every envelope operand is evaluated before the query; `null` or `undefined` collects into a `refuseNode` guard (`errorClass: 'guard'`, step code `NODE_FAILURE`, not routable by a `fault` edge; pinned on update, delete and get, per position, and for a partial filter). An absent variable or key throws from `evaluateValueEnvelope` and the node fails with `EXECUTION_ERROR` before any query; that one IS routable by a `fault` edge, as at every value slot since S1, and routing skips the node — a skipped write is not a widened one. A literal `null` operand is handed on as an authored condition. Keys, operators and combinators are structure and are never evaluated; the resolved filter is a copy. No path drops a condition.

5. **`interpolateFilter` leaves no caller — right.** `git grep` over the head tree finds the symbol only in release-owned CHANGELOGs, in this changeset, in one test comment and in a pin asserting its absence. The `isKnownFilterToken` import leaves `template.ts` with it.

6. **The retirement of `flow-filter-token-unknown` and its three `@objectstack/lint` exports — right: a correct application of one judge per position; no maintainer decision is needed.** The rule's premise was the executor's two-layer dispatch at a flow filter (`resolveToken` first, hand-off second). S6 removes that dispatch under the ruling's "one dialect per slot" and ADR-0032 Decision 3 / Sequencing 6, so the premise no longer exists, and the rule's own hint prescribed the refused dialect (`write {NAME() + 7}`, `or use a filter placeholder`). Every string it could flag at a CRUD filter is now refused earlier and wider (every `{…}` token, not only the unknown-function arm), at `error`, at the same doors plus the contract parse, with the envelope remedy. Coverage check: its walk (`scanForFilters` over `FILTER_KEYS`) also reached a `filter`-keyed value on a non-CRUD node, but no evaluator ever ran there, so its message ("the evaluator raises a guard refusal and this node cannot run") was false at those positions; nothing true is lost. Neither this repository nor the pinned objectui tree imports `validateFlowFilterTokens`, `FLOW_FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` or `FlowFilterTokenFinding`, so the Console Pin Gate cannot be reached by the removal. It is declared in the `Clause-②` narrowing arm and carried by the `@objectstack/lint` `major`. One prose gap, carried in ③: the changeset does not name the id a machine consumer now sees (`expression-invalid`).

7. **The published JSON Schemas for `GetRecordConfig`, `UpdateRecordConfig` and `DeleteRecordConfig` — right, with the gap named.** The published `filter` stays a record of string to any; it gains the operand description, the `xExpression: 'value'` marker (declared to the ledger ratchet), and a new `x-dropped-refinements` site `filter` on each — three new rows in the hand-edited `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (232 → 234 schemas, 752 → 755 sites). A `superRefine` does not project, so each JSON file is wider than its Zod and an author validating against it learns of the token refusal from the description alone. That is the route S1–S5 took (`UpdateRecordConfig` `fields.valueType`, `HttpConfig`), not a new kind of gap; teaching the projection list a named pattern stays a separate public-contract decision. The checked-in `json-schema.manifest/automation.json` lists names only, so it rightly does not move. The generated reference page carries the same text.

8. **The `dialect`-named-field corner — right, documented, and the escape works by construction.** `flowFilterOperands` reads an object at a field's value that names a string `dialect` as an envelope, so a nested-relation condition `{ rel: { dialect: 'x' } }` is refused as a malformed envelope; the top-level filter is never an operand, so a top-level field named `dialect` is unaffected. The escape `{ rel: { dialect: { $eq: 'x' } } }` is an operator map (the value is not a string and the inner key starts with `$`) and walks to a literal operand. 0 such fields in the repository; the changeset and the flows guide both state it.

9. **The remaining public-surface changes are the declared ones.** New `@objectstack/spec` exports `flowFilterOperands`, `FlowFilterOperand`, `classifyFlowFilterOperandString` and `FlowFilterOperandStringKind` (api-surface and export-origins, +4 each); the optional `FlowNodeExpressionPath.filterOperands` and `ValueSlotTemplateOptions.filterOperand` (widening); three `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` rows; `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` gains `get_record` and `delete_record`; the three descriptors' `filter` descriptions, `CRUD_RECORD_ID_GUIDANCE` and the run-user remedy restated (refusal text, not accept set); `flow-template-grammar.ts` keeps every export with its header re-judged. The migrations in examples, docs, dogfood fixtures and tests are envelopes or kept placeholders; two example pins were re-judged honestly (`loop-body-iteration` now asserts the evaluation fault on the unbound `currentTask`, still before any query). No skipped test; no weakened expectation outside the deleted rule's own test file.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/19939-flow-crud-filter-operands.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/lint` at `major`; `.changeset/pre.json` on the head is `mode: pre`, `tag: next`, so the three publish on the v18 `next` pre line — the right level for a narrowing on a published authoring surface and a removed export.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: … ; widening: …)`: the arm reader takes the first word of the parenthetical, so the line reads as `yes` with the `narrowing` arm — BREAKING, which the `major` bumps and the `**BREAKING**` banner match. Every item of the narrowing arm and of the widening arm is present in the diff (checked one by one against ① 1–9), and no accept-set change in the diff is missing from the line.
- ADR-0087: the marker reads `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused)`; that entry exists at the merge base and is amended in the diff (surface, replacement, reason and acceptance each gain the filter-operand clauses, and the placeholders are named as kept). No new D3 and no D2 — right: there is no lossless spelling (the template erased and refused where CEL faults on an absent root, and the shadowing case cannot be converted without knowing intent), and no key is removed, so no tombstone.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The decision (the lint rule retires):** answered in ① 6 — right, not an escalation.
- **The deviation:** the permission check refused one `git checkout SHA -- path` restore; the dev reverted with the editor and proved an empty diff against the merge base — a local edit inside the dev's own worktree, in line with the repo's preference for not restoring from a ref, with no external write. The second (a trailer amended before its push) rewrote nothing pushed; every PR commit carries the model-free trailer pair or, on the merges, none. Accepted.
- **The seat-carried pending changesets** (`19939-flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` with "A `filter` value keeps the template dialect"; the run-user changeset's `{uid}` row; the two `22161-lint-slice-*` entries describing the retired rule): real contradictions that ship in the same `18.0.0-next` CHANGELOG if left. A prose face, outside this record's verdict; carrier: the seat's in-place correction (S7), which should land before the first `next` publish that includes S6. Fold into it the gap from ① 6: one line naming `expression-invalid` as the id, and `validateStackExpressions` / `ExprIssue` as the exports, that a consumer keyed on `flow-filter-token-unknown`, `validateFlowFilterTokens` or `FlowFilterTokenFinding` moves to.
- **The skills text** (`skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md:168` names the retired rule; the automation skill's single-brace lines): a governed Tier H surface, rightly left out of this PR; carrier #22585. After S6 that line teaches an id that no longer exists.
- **The out-of-scope class (a) finding** (four spec repo-project tree walks read the gitignored `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/`): not this change's, invisible to CI's fresh checkout, no bearing on this verdict; the seat files it.
- **S7's tails:** `validate-flow-template-paths` still path-checks a single-brace token at a filter operand (14 + 1 fixtures); the lint's bare-`$` hint still prescribes `{x}` at a plugin node's config (pinned as such); the migration registry's step-18 text-slot sentence still says every other flow string keeps the single brace; the lookup-hop clause no longer prints at this position. All within the stage plan's S7 scope; none contradicts S6.
- **The governed-path reading on `skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md`:** the content is the pure regeneration the diff implies. The generator (`build-skill-references.ts`) resolves local imports recursively from each skill's core files; the net diff adds exactly one new import edge inside that closure — `flow-value-slot-template.ts` to `data/context-tokens.zod.ts`, which itself imports `data/date-macros.zod.ts` — and the two added lines are those two files' pointers, with their module-doc first lines verbatim, at the generator's sort position. No `SKILL_MAP` or `TRANSITIVE_ALLOWLIST` edit is in the net diff, and the generator script is not in the PR's file list. The predicate itself is the seat's to re-read.
- **Check-runs on the head, as read at 2026-10-13T04:36Z:** 39 runs — 27 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 7 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6 and `Type Check · workspace`), 0 red. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Type Check · consumer gates` are green. The seat's pre-queue check ② waits on the seven to conclude; this record does not wait on them. `mergeable_state` reads `blocked` (draft).
